coverage.target: NFR1 (feed content displays within 2 seconds) is specifically FeedUnit's request path; SuggestionUnit shares no request path with the feed's content-display flow
NFR3 (payment-data handling) belongs to donation-unit; SuggestionUnit has no payment surface
NFR4.1 (data protection — the one Unit whose content is intentionally non-public/Confidential rather than public)

NFR5 (payment reconciliation — a timeout is never treated as a success/failure without checking the aggregator's record) is specifically donation-unit's concern; SuggestionUnit has no payment surface. Its own rate-limit enforcement (NFR-RATE.1) reuses the SAME atomic-conditional-write technique NFR5's reconciliation work established project-wide, but that is a shared engineering pattern, not coverage of NFR5's actual subject matter — marked N/A rather than OK to avoid the fabricated-coverage mistake auth-unit's review (R-06) caught
NFR6.1 (services/-layer access boundary and mandatory self-review before merging authorization/rate-limit changes)
Accessibility (WCAG AA baseline) is a UI-rendering concern owned by flutter-app-unit; SuggestionUnit has no UI of its own
Testing methodology/coverage floor is a cross-cutting Build and Test concern, not a Unit-level NFR target

note: performance-requirements.md (NFR-PERF.1-2), scalability-requirements.md (NFR-SC.1), and observability-requirements.md (NFR-OBS.1-5) are intentionally outside the NFR1-NFR8 inheritance chain above: inception's requirements.md defines no performance/scalability/observability NFR for this Unit's own request paths, so these files use Unit-local IDs rather than a fabricated inception sub-ID.
